rules: ADD quantity multiplies by sold quantity and allowed option quantity.
REMOVE subtracts target line quantity divided by recipe yield for each sold unit. It does not remove the whole batch quantity.
REPLACE removes the same per-sold-unit target amount and adds quantity_per_sold_unit of the replacement ingredient.
REMOVE and REPLACE are single-selection effects unless a separately specified rule makes repetition unambiguous. Reject conflicting selected effects on the same target line.
An effect must not drive a base ingredient line below zero.
No match is not equivalent to no effect. Unmapped options relevant to consumption must remain an exception.
The new effect contract requires Phase 2 implementation; existing modifier master-data references alone do not prove operational stock handling.

Component option defaults and selectable substitutions require explicit rules; do not infer them from labels.
Scope and version
Workbook contract v1.0, 16 November 2026. It combines verified existing QOS entities and proposed Phase 2/3 inputs. It contains no live export of your existing catalogue.
Current upload profile

Use the separate QOS_Current_Catalogue_Import.csv or save only Current Import as CSV UTF-8. The current XLSX parser reads the first worksheet only, has a 2 MiB file limit, 500 data rows, 32 columns and 2,000 characters per cell. The full workbook requires a new profile.
Tenant and brand

Select the authorised tenant and brand in QOS before preview. Exports must include their identity as immutable manifest context. Do not accept another tenant’s IDs or assign data through display names alone. Quotes is the first customer, not a global tenant default.
Current profile identity

source_id is scoped by tenant and connection key. Retain both source ID and connection key for repeat imports. It is not the QOS ID. A missing source link is treated as a create; the current profile does not match an existing manually created product merely by name or SKU.
Current profile applied fields

The parser recognises 13 mappings, but the inspected apply path writes the narrower seven-column profile supplied here: source_id, internal_name, English/Arabic names, amount_minor, currency on create and image_url. Parsed descriptions, SKU/barcode and variant labels are not persisted by this path; use the expanded sheets for their proposed future import. Keep currency aligned with the existing price on updates. Existing non-null SKU/barcode can still cause an Update preview because comparison and apply differ; inspect the preview.
Image changes

Current flat-profile imports normally preserve an approved primary image unless explicit re-ingestion is enabled. A different image URL alone is not a verified replacement operation. The expanded profile must preview keep, replace, failed ingestion and retry states without discarding a valid existing asset.
Expanded profile identity

Workbook keys link rows; exported qos_* identifiers identify existing records. Keep both stable. expected_revision is an export/preview token that the proposed importer must check. Never match updates solely on product names.
Create and update

For the expanded profile: create needs the required fields; update needs the exported QOS ID/revision and intended changed values. Blank optional UPDATE cells mean unchanged. Explicit clear_fields names the optional fields to clear. All these action semantics require implementation.
Omission and archive

An omitted row does nothing. Archive is explicit and only supported where the domain service permits it. Product Categories, Product Modifiers and Menu Branches use remove_link for a reviewed detach. Posted opening stock is corrected by reversal/adjustment, never by archive or overwrite.
Drafts and publication

Import applies permitted changes to drafts through existing QOS services. Translation approval, publication, activation and operational posting remain separate authorised actions. A status cell cannot approve Arabic content or publish a menu.
Price units

Existing menu prices and modifier deltas use integer minor units: AED 20.00 = 2000. Proposed ingredient reference costs use decimal major currency units per storage unit. Do not mix these two conventions. Numeric zero is a real value; blank means unknown.
Currencies and tax

AED is the Quotes pilot currency in this template. Other tenants need a currency-aware template profile. Price tax basis/rate are explicitly proposed fields. Confirm tax and net-cost treatment before comparing ingredient cost with selling price.
Units and conversions

Ingredient factor means recipe units per one storage unit. Example format: 1 kg = 1000 g; a pack may be 12 pieces for one ingredient only. Do not assume mass-to-volume or universal pack conversions. Recipe-line quantities use the ingredient’s declared recipe unit.
Recipes and yields

Recipe line quantities describe the full stated yield. Divide each line by the positive recipe yield to obtain usage per sale/output unit. Resolve versions and effective dates; never rewrite posted historical consumption when a current recipe changes.
Modifier effects

ADD quantities are per sold unit per selected option quantity. REMOVE/REPLACE targets one base recipe line. Convert its batch amount using yield; reject conflicts, double replacements and negative consumption. Current modifier pricing/rules remain separate.
Reference costing

Ingredient costs in the workbook are dated onboarding/reference inputs, not a perpetual valuation engine. Missing cost remains unavailable. Actual stock valuation uses accepted receipts, opening balances and the agreed QOS cost policy.
Prep versus production

Recipe reading, checklists, batch calculation, preparation targets and observed counts do not post stock. Actual raw-input consumption and prepared-output production transactions are Phase 3. No double consumption on later sales.
Opening stock

Opening Stock is a separate transaction intake, not generic menu/master-data apply. QOS must validate branch, warehouse, units, cutoff, quantity, cost, source and duplicate protection, then ask for posting confirmation. Corrections use traceable reversal/adjustment.
Later fields

Future Combos and Combo Components are fixed-composition proposals for Phase 3. free_options_count is an unscheduled later pricing proposal, not a Phase 2 commitment. Unsupported populated fields must be identified as deferred/rejected, never silently dropped or treated as applied.
Availability

Existing branch availability is controlled through stop-sales and schedules, not a fictional generic branch-offer table. This workbook captures branch price overrides; preserve and review availability through existing QOS controls.
Branch price resets

Branch Prices uses reset_to_central for a reviewed removal of an override, following the existing price-reset audit model. The result inherits the current central price. Branches are suspended with status=suspended; they do not use an invented archive operation.
Branch mapping

Dubai, Al Ain and Azur Cafe are requested business labels. Historical QOS branches HBZ Stadium, HCT Academic City and Al Ain Zoo must be mapped deliberately. Do not rename IDs or reassign history automatically.
External mapping

Provider IDs remain distinct from QOS IDs and workbook keys. Include connection/provider/entity/branch context. Foodics and Loyverse mapping is proposed Phase 2 data; credentials never belong in this workbook.
Validation coverage

Dropdowns and row checks catch basic input mistakes only. Reference review can mean a record exists in QOS but is not listed here. QOS must verify types, references, permissions, versions, conditional fields, full business rules and supported capabilities.
Recovery and repeat upload

Preview before apply. Report created, updated, unchanged, skipped, failed and deferred rows. Resume/retry without duplicate records. Current implementation does not establish workbook-wide atomicity; do not display partial work as a full success.
Capacity and export

Input tables reserve 100 rows by default; larger tables reserve 200 and Current Import reserves 500. To extend them, extend the table, validations, reference ranges and row-check formulas together. Future QOS exports should size these automatically.
Real data and account access

Enter confirmed operational information only. There are no sample customer rows. Keep account passwords, PINs, API tokens and credentials outside this workbook. User invitations and access remain in QOS administration.
Separate transaction contracts

Daily sales, tenders, receipts, waste and counts are Phase 2 UI/import workflows described in the Claude brief. They are not mixed into the menu master-data tables. Purchase orders, transfers and production posting are later workflows.

ingredient_cost_per_recipe_unit.guards: Cost is explicitly numeric, factor is numeric and > 0, currency/date match the required cost basis. Missing cost yields unavailable, never zero. All summed costs must use the same confirmed NET or GROSS tax basis, normalized explicitly before comparison. An unconfirmed basis cannot produce a claimed net ingredient margin.
ingredient_cost_per_recipe_unit.meaning: Planning/reference cost only; not a stock valuation engine.

recipe_line_cost.guards: Resolve one exact ingredient key; all required numeric inputs known; matching currency/effective date. All summed costs must use the same confirmed NET or GROSS tax basis, normalized explicitly before comparison. An unconfirmed basis cannot produce a claimed net ingredient margin.

recipe_cost_per_yield_unit.expression: SUM(recipe_line_cost for every line in the version) / yield_quantity
recipe_cost_per_yield_unit.guards: Yield > 0, at least one line, and every required line fully costed. If any cost is missing, show incomplete cost rather than a partial total labelled complete. All summed costs must use the same confirmed NET or GROSS tax basis, normalized explicitly before comparison. An unconfirmed basis cannot produce a claimed net ingredient margin.

sale_consumption.expression: Base quantity for an ingredient line = sold_quantity × quantity_recipe_units / yield_quantity; then apply validated option effects exactly once.
sale_consumption.guards: Accepted recipe/version and option mapping; compatible sale/yield units; no duplicate sales source event; conflicting effects remain exceptions.

prepared_reference_cost_per_storage_unit.phase: Phase 3 operational costing; Phase 2 guidance can show an explicitly labelled estimate only
prepared_reference_cost_per_storage_unit.expression: SUM(input recipe line reference costs) / prepared recipe yield_quantity × prepared ingredient.recipe_units_per_storage_unit
prepared_reference_cost_per_storage_unit.guards: Acyclic graph, correct output units, complete costs. Actual production valuation uses actual posted inputs/output and agreed policy. All summed costs must use the same confirmed NET or GROSS tax basis, normalized explicitly before comparison. An unconfirmed basis cannot produce a claimed net ingredient margin.

opening_value.guards: Known quantity and cost in same storage unit/currency; positive quantity with unknown cost cannot show a completed valuation.

profileCoverage.included: Catalogue definitions, Phase 2 setup/recipe definitions, separately reviewed opening-stock intake, external mapping preparation and deferred fixed-composition combo definitions.
uiOnlyInPhase2: shared recipe assignments beyond the primary variant target
profileCoverage.excluded: Live POS credentials; users/passwords; purchase-order, transfer and production transaction imports.
profileCoverage.calculationImplementation: XLSX formulas provide readiness checks/counts only. Cost/consumption/valuation expressions specify proposed QOS functionality, not implemented spreadsheet calculations.
